summary: Closed the three obligations the code review raised and changed nothing else. T-005 (O-028): the hook now probes the UI thread every 10 ms, not every 50 ms, and T-005 checks p95 < 200 ms only in phases with at least 20 probes, keeping max < 1000 ms. Every asserted phase had 54–143 probes, and T-005 passed 4 of 4 runs. Tree size (O-029): while the tree is shown, the outcome and results rows split 1:3 instead of 3:1, and the default window height is 860 px instead of 620, clamped to the work area. At startup the window is moved up if Windows placed its bottom below the work area. The tree's default viewport went from 39 px to 284 px (14 rows). Unreadable folders (O-030): B-007 now reads the tree through the hook and checks that each of the 12 denied folders draws no expander, 0 bytes, 0.0 % and 'could not be opened'; a folder whose listing failed partway now reads 'could not be read in full'. All 34 window cases, the 240 Core tests, the hook cases and the rule checks passed, and the published exe on C:\Program Files behaved as expected.

files.why: O-029: Height 860 (MinHeight stays 620). A MultiDataTrigger on each results-grid row makes the split 1* outcome / 3* results while FolderTree is visible, keeping both row MinHeights (292, 84); after a stop or failure it stays 3:1. The layout comment is updated.

O-029: the constructor clamps Height to SystemParameters.WorkArea.Height. OnSourceInitialized moves the window up when Windows' cascade placed its bottom below the work area (measured 62 px over on 3 of 10 launches before the fix, none after).
O-030: an Unreadable folder notes 'could not be opened' when it has no rows, and 'could not be read in full' when its listing failed partway and it kept rows (ChildCount > 0).

O-028: the GAP probe runs every 10 ms. The gap lines log when the longest wait was posted, a rescan-started line logs how long StartScan held the UI thread, and the ending lines log the first move time, the longest move, the tree viewport, and the window's top and height against the work area (used by B-007's window checks).

O-028: T-005 checks p95 only with >= 20 probes ($GapP95Floor), always checks max < 1000, and prints probe counts, move and StartScan timings. O-030/O-029: new CheckTopsTree, run first in B-007 through tree mode with FSA_HOOK_WALK=1. It asserts the 12 denied folders and the 24 other folders, a default window of 860 px (or the work area) inside the work area, and at least 12 tree rows in view. B-007's default-size label now reads 880 by 860. T-003's second run is at the work area's height with the precondition 'more room than the default', because 1,000 px no longer gives twice the new default.

Records the tree's room (1:3 split, 860 default, move-up), the note wording, the T-005 p95 rule and B-007's tree read. Corrects the first build's row-6 claim (47 ms), which the review could not reproduce, and gives this build's measurements. Records the display-state-dependent resize stall. The 'two rows' finding is marked as resolved.

obligations.how: The hook's probe runs every 10 ms, so each asserted phase had 54–143 probes (at least 40, as the fix asked). T-005 checks p95 < 200 ms only where a phase has >= 20 probes, prints 'p95 not asserted' otherwise, and always checks max < 1000 ms. Four runs passed. In one display state (3 runs), the longest waits were 380–467 ms in the first scan and 709–857 ms in the rescan, with p95 at most 71 ms. In the other (the All run), the longest wait was 68 ms. The doc corrects the first build's '47 ms' claim, and the stall is recorded as a follow-up for SL-039/SL-040's window.

While FolderTree is visible, the outcome and results rows split 1:3 via MultiDataTriggers, keeping MinHeight 292 and 84. The default Height is 860, clamped to the work area, and MinHeight stays 620. The window is also moved up if it opens below the work area. At the default size the tree has a 284 px viewport (14 full rows), up from 39 px, and the report shows FolderTree 288 px with 14 full rows. B-007 (label updated to 880 by 860) and B-008 were re-run in the All run and passed; at the minimum size every list still has a full row.

B-007 now starts with a tree-mode read (FSA_HOOK_WALK=1) of New-TopsTree's completed scan. Each of the 12 b*-folders draws no expander, 0 bytes, '0.0 %' and 'could not be opened'. The other 24 folders can be opened and have no note, and the root has no note. It passed in two B-007 runs and in the All run. FolderTreeNode.Note now reads 'could not be read in full' when an Unreadable folder has ChildCount > 0. No window case covers that branch, because an ordinary user cannot make a real listing fail partway (see not_built).

Owed to validate-slice, not this stage. The release precondition is exercised by T-004: a WeakReference to the first store, a depth-3 row selected, a 3,000-row folder open. T-004 passed again in this build's All run. An at-scale re-measure of the 1 GiB budget stays an open follow-up from attempt 1.

deviations: The window is moved up at startup (MainWindow.OnSourceInitialized) when Windows placed its bottom below the work area; the fix only said to clamp the height. Clamping alone was not enough: over 10 cascaded launches, an 860 px window's bottom fell 10, 36 and 62 px below the 1,032 px work area on 3 of them, cutting off the tree's last rows. With the move-up, all 10 fit.

T-003's second run is now at the work area's height (FSA_HOOK_HEIGHT=4000, clamped to the work area) instead of 1,000 px, and its precondition changed from 'more than twice the default viewport' to 'more room than the default'. The new default gives the tree 284 px, and 1,000 px does not give twice that. The work area gave 456 px (46 rows built), and the cold open took 141.9 ms.

T-005 has no hard 'at least 40 probes' check. The 40-probe target is met by the 10 ms sampling rate (54–143 probes in every asserted phase over 4 runs). The assertion follows the decided rule: p95 only with >= 20 probes, and max < 1000 always.

The hook logs diagnostics the fix did not name: when each phase's longest wait was posted, the first move time and longest move, how long StartScan held the UI thread, and the tree viewport and window geometry on the ending lines. B-007 needs the geometry to check the default size. The timings were needed to attribute the resize stall: StartScan, including the release of a 100,000-row open folder, took 2.8–7.4 ms, so the stall is not the tree's release.
not_built: No window case covers the 'could not be read in full' wording for a folder whose listing failed partway (Scanner.cs:158-166). Window cases drive a real scan of a real NTFS tree, and an ordinary user cannot make a directory listing fail partway. The 'could not be opened' branch is covered by B-007's 12 denied folders.

As in attempt 1, the design's Case D re-run of the StallRig network cases (N-001..N-004) was not run. They create and remove SMB client mappings on this machine, which I may not change; they are person-run with -IncludeNetwork.
follow_ups: For SL-039/SL-040's window: moving and resizing the window while a scan starts can block the UI thread for most of a second, depending on the display state. In T-005's shape here, one batch of runs had longest waits of 361–467 ms in the first scan and 378–857 ms in the rescan, and every hand-off peaked at 105–136 ms. Minutes later, the same runs had no wait over 98 ms and moves of at most 28 ms, whether a 100,000-row or a 1-row folder was open before the rescan. The review measured 419–511 ms in the pre-slice exe (de51999) and no stall without moves. T-005 now logs when the longest wait was posted and how long each move took, for whoever investigates.
Add a Core test seam, or a scanner-level test, for a listing that fails partway, so the tree's 'could not be read in full' row (an expander over the listed rows) can get a window case.
The attempt-1 follow-up about the tree's two-row viewport at 880x620 is resolved by O-029 (284 px, 14 rows by default) and can be closed.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 build FsAnalyser.slnx -c Release --nologo -v q
tests.note: 0 warnings, 0 errors, built twice (after the first edits and at the end).

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests -c Release --no-build --nologo

tests.note: Run twice. The tree read showed 37 rows, all drawn, and each of the 12 b*-folders with no expander, 0 bytes, 0.0 % and 'could not be opened'. The window was 860 px tall, top 78 then 172 in a 1,032 px work area, with a 284 px viewport. At the default size the report showed FolderTree 288 px with 14 full rows; at the minimum size 48 px with 2 full rows.

Three runs, all passed, in the display state where the review saw failures. Probes per phase: scan 54–59, handoff 59–73, rescan 54–56, rescan-handoff 58–59. p95: scan 62–64 ms, rescan 64–71 ms. Longest waits: scan 380–467 ms, rescan 709–857 ms, all under the 1,000 ms limit.

tests.command: Published exe launched 10 times under FSA_HOOK_MODE=tree FSA_HOOK_WALK=0 on a small temp tree, window position logged
tests.note: Before the move-up fix, Windows cascaded the window's top from 26 to 234 px, so an 860 px window's bottom reached 1,042, 1,068 and 1,094 px against a 1,032 px work area. This led to OnSourceInitialized's move-up. After the fix, the same 10 launches all fit: the overflowing ones sat at top 172 with the bottom at 1,032.

tests.command: Published exe under FSA_HOOK_MODE=tree FSA_HOOK_GAP=deep|big on a T-005-shaped temp tree, two batches
tests.note: Diagnostic experiment, not a gate. Batch 1: rescan longest wait 378–481 ms with deep open, 393–844 ms with big open. Batch 2, minutes later: 17–39 ms either way, StartScan 2.8–7.4 ms, 22 moves per scan at most 27 ms each. Conclusion: the stall depends on the display state, not on the tree.

All 34 cases passed: C-001..C-014, O-016, L-001..L-003, B-001..B-008, V-001, P-001, T-001..T-006. T-003: cold open 97.9 ms at the default size (284 px, 29 rows built), warm 1.6–2.7 ms; at the work area's height 141.9 ms (456 px, 46 rows). T-005: 64–143 probes per phase, longest wait 68 ms outside the open, p95 0.4–11.5 ms. T-002: 1,281 px of rows in a 284 px viewport. N-001..N-004 were not run (person-run network cases).
H-001 and H-002 passed with the changed hook.
AGREE 11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns; 28 settled entries.
rules-parity: AGREE. I also ran by hand the settled .taad/fitness.yaml rule patterns covering the touched files: MainWindow.xaml(.cs), FolderTreeNode.cs and TreeMode.cs. No match.

Real input through the real entry point: exit 0 after 4 s. 54 rows walked, 0 undrawn. The root (31.8 GB) equals the sum of its 53 rows (34,154,406,672 bytes on disk). The top row is NVIDIA GPU Computing Toolkit, 4.8 GB, 15.1 %. WindowsApps is noted 'could not be opened' with no expander. The window was 860 px tall at top 172, and the tree had a 284 px viewport.

The way validate reads the window: EXIT 0, Completed. FolderTree was visible and in view, 288.3 px, 14 full rows. LargestFilesList was 76 px with 3 full rows, the outcome panel 276 px, TopLevelList not shown.
